records.name: QLS.Stoch.robbinsSiegmund_expBound
records.entry_name: ArtificialTheorems
records.statement:
theorem robbinsSiegmund_expBound.{v}
    {Ω : Type v} [m0 : MeasurableSpace Ω]
    (μ : Measure Ω) [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    (ℱ : Filtration ℕ m0)
    (X Y Z W : ℕ → Ω → ℝ)
    (adapted_X : Adapted ℱ X) (adapted_Y : Adapted ℱ Y)
    (adapted_Z : Adapted ℱ Z) (adapted_W : Adapted ℱ W)
    (predictable_Y : Adapted ℱ fun t => Y (t + 1))
    (predictable_Z : Adapted ℱ fun t => Z (t + 1))
    (predictable_W : Adapted ℱ fun t => W (t + 1))
    (hX_nonneg : ∀ t ω, 0 ≤ X t ω)
    (hY_nonneg : ∀ t ω, 0 ≤ Y t ω)
    (hZ_nonneg : ∀ t ω, 0 ≤ Z t ω)
    (hW_nonneg : ∀ t ω, 0 ≤ W t ω)
    (condexp_ineq : ∀ t,
      μ[fun ω => X (t + 1) ω | ℱ t]
        ≤ᵐ[μ] fun ω => (1 + Y (t + 1) ω) * X t ω + Z (t + 1) ω - W (t + 1) ω)
    (integrable_X : ∀ t, Integrable (X t) μ)
    (integrable_Z : ∀ t, Integrable (Z t) μ)
    (integrable_W : ∀ t, Integrable (W t) μ)
    (sumEZ : Summable (fun t => ∫ ω, Z t ω ∂μ))
    (prod_bound : ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ t ω, prodY Y t ω ≤ C)
  : ∃ Xlim : Ω → ℝ,
      (∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun t => X t ω) atTop (nhds (Xlim ω))) ∧
      (∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Summable (fun t => W t ω)) := by
  sorry
records.doc:
Robbins–Siegmund variant under expectation-level summability and a uniform product bound.

Assumptions:
- Adaptedness/predictability for `X,Y,Z,W` as in the main theorem
- Nonnegativity: `0 ≤ X t ω, 0 ≤ Y t ω, 0 ≤ Z t ω, 0 ≤ W t ω`
- Integrability: `X t, Z t, W t` integrable for all `t`
- Drift: `μ[X_{t+1} | ℱ_t] ≤ (1+Y_{t+1}) X_t + Z_{t+1} - W_{t+1}` a.e.
- Expectation summability: `Summable (fun t => ∫ ω, Z t ω ∂μ)`
- Product bound: `∃ C > 0, ∀ t ω, prodY Y t ω ≤ C`

Conclusions:
- `X t` converges almost surely to a finite limit
- `∑ W t` is finite almost surely

signoffs.comment: S. Gadat, Lecture notes on Stochastic Optimization Algorithms, http://perso.math.univ-toulouse.fr/gadat/files/2012/12/cours_Algo_Stos_M2R5.pdf

records.name: QLS.Stoch.robbinsSiegmund_full
records.entry_name: ArtificialTheorems
records.statement:
theorem robbinsSiegmund_full.{v}
    {Ω : Type v} [m0 : MeasurableSpace Ω]
    (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (ℱ : Filtration ℕ m0)
    (V U α β : ℕ → Ω → ℝ)
    -- Adaptedness
    (adapted_V : Adapted ℱ V)
    (adapted_α : Adapted ℱ α)
    (adapted_β : Adapted ℱ β)
    (adapted_U : Adapted ℱ U)
    -- Predictability (X_{n+1} is F_n-measurable)
    (predictable_α : Adapted ℱ fun t => α (t + 1))
    (predictable_β : Adapted ℱ fun t => β (t + 1))
    (predictable_U : Adapted ℱ fun t => U (t + 1))
    -- Nonnegativity
    (hV_nonneg : ∀ t ω, 0 ≤ V t ω)
    (hα_nonneg : ∀ t ω, 0 ≤ α t ω)
    (hβ_nonneg : ∀ t ω, 0 ≤ β t ω)
    (hU_nonneg : ∀ t ω, 0 ≤ U t ω)
    -- Integrability
    (integrable_V : ∀ t, Integrable (V t) μ)
    (integrable_β : ∀ t, Integrable (β t) μ)
    (integrable_U : ∀ t, Integrable (U t) μ)
    -- (ii) Product bound and β summability
    (prod_bound : ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ t ω, prodY α t ω ≤ C)
    (sum_Eβ : Summable (fun t => ∫ ω, β t ω ∂μ))
    -- (iii) Drift inequality
    (condexp_ineq : ∀ t,
      μ[fun ω => V (t + 1) ω | ℱ t]
        ≤ᵐ[μ] fun ω => (1 + α (t + 1) ω) * V t ω + β (t + 1) ω - U (t + 1) ω)
  : -- Conclusions
    -- (a) V_n → V_∞ a.s. with V_∞ ∈ L¹, and sup E[V_n] < ∞
    (∃ Vlim : Ω → ℝ,
      Integrable Vlim μ ∧
      (∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun t => V t ω) atTop (nhds (Vlim ω)))) ∧
    (BddAbove (Set.range fun n => ∫ ω, V n ω ∂μ)) ∧
    -- (b) ∑ U_n < ∞ a.s.
    (∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Summable (fun t => U t ω)) := by
  sorry
records.doc:
Full Robbins-Siegmund theorem with L¹ limit and sup E[V] bound.

Assumptions:
- Adaptedness/predictability for `V, α, β, U`
- Nonnegativity: `0 ≤ V t ω, 0 ≤ α t ω, 0 ≤ β t ω, 0 ≤ U t ω`
- Integrability: `V t, β t, U t` integrable for all `t`
- Product bound: `∃ C > 0, ∀ t ω, prodY α t ω ≤ C`
- Summability: `Summable (fun t => ∫ ω, β t ω ∂μ)`
- Drift inequality: `μ[V_{t+1} | ℱ_t] ≤ (1+α_{t+1}) V_t + β_{t+1} - U_{t+1}` a.e.

Conclusions:
- `V_n → V_∞` a.s. with `V_∞ ∈ L¹`
- `sup E[V_n] < ∞`
- `∑ U_n < ∞` a.s.

signoffs.comment: S. Gadat, Lecture notes on Stochastic Optimization Algorithms, http://perso.math.univ-toulouse.fr/gadat/files/2012/12/cours_Algo_Stos_M2R5.pdf

records.name: convergence_stochastic_gradient_method
records.entry_name: ArtificialTheorems
records.statement:
theorem convergence_stochastic_gradient_method
    (X : ℕ → Ω → E) (γ : ℕ → ℝ) (h : E → E) (ΔM R : ℕ → Ω → E) (V : E → ℝ) (gradV : E → E)
    (ℱ : Filtration ℕ m0)
    (proc : StochasticAlgorithm X γ h ΔM R)
    (asm : SGD_Convergence_Assumptions μ X γ h ΔM R V gradV ℱ) :
    -- (a) sup E[V(X_n)] < +∞
    (BddAbove (Set.range fun n => ∫ ω, V (X n ω) ∂μ)) ∧
    -- (b) ∑ γ_{n+1}⟨∇V, h⟩(X_n) < +∞ a.s.
    (∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Summable (fun n => γ (n + 1) * @inner ℝ _ _ (gradV (X n ω)) (h (X n ω)))) ∧
    -- (c) V(X_n) → V_∞ ∈ L¹ a.s.
    (∃ V_inf : Ω → ℝ, Integrable V_inf μ ∧
      ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => V (X n ω)) atTop (nhds (V_inf ω))) ∧
    -- (d) X_{n+1} - X_n → 0 a.s. and in L²
    (∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => X (n + 1) ω - X n ω) atTop (nhds 0)) ∧
    (Tendsto (fun n => ∫ ω, ‖X (n + 1) ω - X n ω‖^2 ∂μ) atTop (nhds 0)) := by
  sorry
records.doc:
Theorem 2.3.6: Convergence of the Stochastic Gradient Method.

Under assumptions (H1) and (H2), one has:
(a) sup_{n≥0} E[V(X_n)] < +∞
(b) ∑_{n≥0} γ_{n+1}⟨∇V, h⟩(X_n) < +∞ a.s.
(c) V(X_n) → V_∞ ∈ L¹ a.s.
(d) X_n - X_{n-1} → 0 a.s. and in L²

records.name: SGDUniqueMin.convergence_simplified
records.entry_name: ArtificialTheorems
records.statement:
theorem convergence_simplified
    (X : ℕ → Ω → E) (γ : ℕ → ℝ) (h : E → E) (ΔM : ℕ → Ω → E)
    (V : E → ℝ) (gradV : E → E) (ℱ : Filtration ℕ m0) (x_star : E)
    (asm : SimplifiedAssumptions μ X γ h ΔM V gradV ℱ x_star) :
    ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => X n ω) atTop (nhds x_star) := by
  sorry
records.doc:
Simplified Corollary 2.3.1: Almost sure convergence for unbiased SGD with bounded variance.

Under the simplified assumptions (unbiased gradients, constant variance bound), we have:
- X_n → x* almost surely

The proof is simpler because:
1. No remainder term R (so the earlier "line 1375" gap disappears)
2. Constant variance ⟹ E[‖∑ γ_k ΔM_k‖²] ≤ σ² ∑ γ_k² < ∞ directly
3. L²-bounded martingale converges a.s. by Doob's theorem

records.name: VALUE_ITERATION_CONVERGENCE_COMPLETE
records.entry_name: ArtificialTheorems
records.statement:
theorem VALUE_ITERATION_CONVERGENCE_COMPLETE (mdp : MDP S A) (γ : Rat)
    (hγ_nonneg : 0 ≤ γ) (hγ_lt : γ < 1) :
    ∃ v_star : S → ℝ,
    -- 1. v_star is the optimal value function (Bellman equation)
    bellmanOperatorReal mdp γ v_star = v_star ∧
    -- 2. Value iteration converges to v_star from any starting point
    (∀ v₀ : S → Rat, Tendsto (fun n => castToReal ((bellmanOperatorRat mdp γ)^[n] v₀)) atTop (𝓝 v_star)) ∧
    -- 3. Geometric convergence with explicit rate
    (∀ v₀ : S → Rat, ∀ n : ℕ,
      dist (castToReal ((bellmanOperatorRat mdp γ)^[n] v₀)) v_star ≤
      dist v₀ (bellmanOperatorRat mdp γ v₀) * γ^n / (1 - γ)) ∧
    -- 4. Uniqueness: any fixed point of the Bellman operator equals v_star
    (∀ v' : S → ℝ, bellmanOperatorReal mdp γ v' = v' → v' = v_star) := by
  sorry
records.doc: **THE MAIN RESULT**: Value iteration converges with all guarantees

records.name: ApproxValueIterationInt.INT_VALUE_ITERATION_APPROX
records.entry_name: ArtificialTheorems
records.statement:
theorem INT_VALUE_ITERATION_APPROX
    (mdp : MDP S A) (γ : ℚ) (hγ_nonneg : 0 ≤ γ) (hγ_lt : γ < 1) :
    ∃ v_star : S → ℝ,
      bellmanOperatorReal (S:=S) (A:=A) mdp (γ : ℝ) v_star = v_star ∧
      ∀ (v₀ : S → ℤ) (n : ℕ),
        dist (castZtoR ((bellmanOperatorInt (S:=S) (A:=A) mdp γ)^[n] v₀)) v_star
          ≤ (γ : ℝ)^n * dist (castZtoR v₀) v_star +
            ((1 : ℝ) / 2) / (1 - (γ : ℝ)) := by
  sorry
records.doc:
Approximate convergence of integer value iteration.

For discount 0 ≤ γ < 1, the iterate error is bounded by:
  γ^n * dist(v₀, v*) + (1/2) / (1-γ)

records.name: ApproxValueIterationInt.INT_VALUE_ITERATION_EVENTUAL_BALL
records.entry_name: ArtificialTheorems
records.statement:
theorem INT_VALUE_ITERATION_EVENTUAL_BALL
    (mdp : MDP S A) (γ : ℚ) (hγ_nonneg : 0 ≤ γ) (hγ_lt : γ < 1)
    (ε : ℝ) (hε : ((1 : ℝ) / 2) / (1 - (γ : ℝ)) < ε) :
    ∃ v_star : S → ℝ,
      bellmanOperatorReal (S:=S) (A:=A) mdp (γ : ℝ) v_star = v_star ∧
      ∀ v₀ : S → ℤ, ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
        dist (castZtoR ((bellmanOperatorInt (S:=S) (A:=A) mdp γ)^[n] v₀)) v_star ≤ ε := by
  sorry
records.doc:
Eventual ball inclusion.

For any ε > (1/2)/(1-γ), the iterates eventually stay within distance ε of v*.

records.name: universal_approximation_cybenko

theorem universal_approximation_cybenko
    (hJD : HasJordanDecomposition n)
    (σ : ℝ → ℝ) (hσ_cont : Continuous σ) (hσ_sig : IsSigmoidal σ)
    (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → ℝ) (hf_cont : ContinuousOn f (UnitCube n))

records.name: GaussianMeasure.stdGaussianPi
records.entry_name: Lean Statistical Learning Theory
records.statement:
noncomputable def stdGaussianPi (n : ℕ) : Measure (Fin n → ℝ) :=
  Measure.pi fun _ : Fin n => gaussianReal 0 1
records.doc: Standard Gaussian product measure: the product of n independent standard Gaussians N(0,1)

records.name: GaussianMeasure.stdGaussianE
records.entry_name: Lean Statistical Learning Theory
records.statement:
noncomputable def stdGaussianE (n : ℕ) : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :=
  Measure.map (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin n) ℝ).symm (stdGaussianPi n)
records.doc: The standard Gaussian on EuclideanSpace as pushforward of stdGaussianPi via the equivalence.

records.name: IsENet
records.entry_name: Lean Statistical Learning Theory
records.statement:
def IsENet {A : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace A] (t : Finset A) (eps : ℝ) (s : Set A) : Prop :=
  s ⊆ ⋃ x ∈ t, closedBall x eps
records.doc:
`t` is an `eps`-net for `s` if every point of `s` lies in a closed ball of radius `eps`
centered at some element of `t`.

records.name: coveringNumber
records.entry_name: Lean Statistical Learning Theory
records.statement:
noncomputable def coveringNumber {A : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace A] (eps : ℝ) (s : Set A) : WithTop Nat :=
  sInf {n : WithTop Nat | ∃ t : Finset A, IsENet t eps s ∧ (t.card : WithTop Nat) = n}
records.doc: Covering number: the minimal cardinality of a finite `eps`-net, as `WithTop Nat`.

records.name: metricEntropyOfNat
records.entry_name: Lean Statistical Learning Theory
records.statement:
def metricEntropyOfNat (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  if n ≤ 1 then 0 else Real.log n
records.doc: Helper to compute metric entropy given a natural number.

records.name: metricEntropy
records.entry_name: Lean Statistical Learning Theory
records.statement:
def metricEntropy (eps : ℝ) (s : Set A) : ℝ :=
  match _h : coveringNumber eps s with
  | ⊤ => 0
  | (n : ℕ) => metricEntropyOfNat n
records.doc: Metric entropy: log of covering number.

records.name: sqrtEntropy
records.entry_name: Lean Statistical Learning Theory
records.statement:
def sqrtEntropy (eps : ℝ) (s : Set A) : ℝ :=
  Real.sqrt (metricEntropy eps s)
records.doc: Square root of metric entropy.

records.name: dudleyIntegrand
records.entry_name: Lean Statistical Learning Theory
records.statement:
def dudleyIntegrand (eps : ℝ) (s : Set A) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ENNReal.ofReal (sqrtEntropy eps s)
records.doc: Dudley integrand: √(log N(ε, s)) as ENNReal.

records.name: entropyIntegralENNReal
records.entry_name: Lean Statistical Learning Theory
records.statement:
def entropyIntegralENNReal (s : Set A) (D : ℝ) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ∫⁻ eps in Set.Ioc (0 : ℝ) D, dudleyIntegrand eps s
records.doc: Entropy integral (ENNReal): ∫₀^D √(log N(ε, s)) dε.

records.name: entropyIntegral
records.entry_name: Lean Statistical Learning Theory
records.statement:
def entropyIntegral (s : Set A) (D : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (entropyIntegralENNReal s D).toReal
records.doc: Entropy integral (real-valued wrapper).

records.name: IsSubGaussianProcess
records.entry_name: Lean Statistical Learning Theory
records.doc:
A stochastic process X indexed by a metric space is σ-sub-Gaussian if
the MGF of increments satisfies E[exp(l(X_s - X_t))] ≤ exp(l²σ²d(s,t)²/2).

records.name: EfronSteinApp.CompactlySupportedSmooth
records.entry_name: Lean Statistical Learning Theory
records.statement:
def CompactlySupportedSmooth (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ContDiff ℝ 2 f ∧ HasCompactSupport f
records.doc: A function is compactly supported and smooth (C²)

records.name: GaussianLipConcen.gaussian_lipschitz_concentration
records.entry_name: Lean Statistical Learning Theory
records.statement:
theorem gaussian_lipschitz_concentration {f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) → ℝ} {L : ℝ≥0}
    (hn : 0 < n) (hL : 0 < L) (hf : LipschitzWith L f) (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 < t) :
    let μ := stdGaussianE n
    (μ {x | t ≤ |f x - ∫ y, f y ∂μ|}).toReal ≤ 2 * exp (-t^2 / (2 * (L : ℝ)^2)) := by
  sorry
records.doc:
**Gaussian Lipschitz Concentration Inequality**

For any L-Lipschitz function f on ℝⁿ equipped with the standard Gaussian measure,
the probability that f deviates from its mean by more than t is at most
2 exp(-t² / (2L²)).

records.name: dudley
records.entry_name: Lean Statistical Learning Theory
records.statement:
theorem dudley {μ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    {X : A → Ω → ℝ} {σ : ℝ} (hσ : 0 < σ)
    (hX : IsSubGaussianProcess μ X σ)
    {s : Set A} (hs : TotallyBounded s)
    {D : ℝ} (hD : 0 < D) (hdiam : Metric.diam s ≤ D)
    (t₀ : A) (ht₀ : t₀ ∈ s) (hcenter : ∀ ω, X t₀ ω = 0)
    (hX_meas : ∀ t, Measurable (X t))
    (hX_int_exp : ∀ t s : A, ∀ l : ℝ, Integrable (fun ω => Real.exp (l * (X t ω - X s ω))) μ)
    (hfinite : entropyIntegralENNReal s D ≠ ⊤)
    (hcont : ∀ ω, Continuous (fun (t : ↥s) => X t.1 ω)) :
    ∫ ω, ⨆ t ∈ s, X t ω ∂μ ≤ (12 * Real.sqrt 2) * σ * entropyIntegral s D := by
  sorry
records.doc:
**Dudley's Entropy Integral Theorem**

For a σ-sub-Gaussian process X indexed by a totally bounded set s with diameter ≤ D,
the expected supremum satisfies:
  E[sup_{t∈s} X_t] ≤ 12√2 · σ · ∫₀^D √(log N(ε, s)) dε

records.name: efronStein
records.entry_name: Lean Statistical Learning Theory
records.statement:
theorem efronStein (f : (Fin n → Ω) → ℝ) (hf : MemLp f 2 (Measure.pi μs)) :
    variance f (Measure.pi μs) ≤
    ∑ i : Fin n, ∫ x, (f x - condExpExceptCoord (μs := μs) i f x)^2 ∂(Measure.pi μs) := by
  sorry
records.doc:
**Efron-Stein Inequality**

For independent random variables X₁,...,Xₙ and a square-integrable function f:
  Var(f) ≤ ∑ᵢ E[(f - E^{(i)}f)²]
where E^{(i)}f is the conditional expectation given all variables except Xᵢ.

records.name: GaussianPoincare.gaussianPoincare
records.entry_name: Lean Statistical Learning Theory
records.statement:
theorem gaussianPoincare {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : CompactlySupportedSmooth f) :
    variance (fun x => f x) stdGaussianMeasure ≤
    ∫ x, (deriv f x)^2 ∂stdGaussianMeasure := by
  sorry
records.doc:
**Gaussian Poincaré Inequality**

For any f ∈ C²_c(ℝ) and X ~ N(0,1):
  Var(f(X)) ≤ E[f'(X)²]

records.name: networks_exist

records.statement:
theorem networks_exist (n : ℕ) : ∃ net : ComparatorNetwork n, net.Sorts ∧
    net.depth ≤ 141 * 10 ^ 62 * Nat.clog 2 n ∧

records.name: Problem4.harmonic_mean_inequality_full
records.entry_name: Archon FirstProof Results
records.statement:
theorem harmonic_mean_inequality_full
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (p q : ℝ[X])
    (hp_monic : p.Monic) (hq_monic : q.Monic)
    (hp_deg : p.natDegree = n) (hq_deg : q.natDegree = n)
    (hp_real : ∀ z : ℂ, (p.map (algebraMap ℝ ℂ)).IsRoot z → z.im = 0)
    (hq_real : ∀ z : ℂ, (q.map (algebraMap ℝ ℂ)).IsRoot z → z.im = 0) :
    invPhiN_poly n (polyBoxPlus n p q) ≥ invPhiN_poly n p + invPhiN_poly n q := by sorry
records.doc:
**Main Theorem (Problem 4)**: Harmonic-mean inequality for Φₙ under box-plus
    convolution. For monic real-rooted polynomials p, q of degree n ≥ 2:
    1/Φₙ(p ⊞ₙ q) ≥ 1/Φₙ(p) + 1/Φₙ(q)

records.name: Problem6.exists_eps_light_subset
records.entry_name: Archon FirstProof Results
records.statement:
theorem exists_eps_light_subset
    (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (ε : ℝ) (hε_pos : 0 < ε) (hε_le : ε ≤ 1) :
    ∃ S : Finset V, IsEpsLight G ε S ∧
      ε / 256 * (Fintype.card V : ℝ) ≤
      (S.card : ℝ) := by sorry
records.doc:
**Main Theorem (Problem 6)**: For every simple graph G on a finite vertex set V
    and every ε ∈ (0, 1], there exists an ε-light subset S with |S| ≥ ε/256 · |V|.

records.name: Zip.Native.Deflate.inflate_deflateRaw

theorem inflate_deflateRaw (data : ByteArray) (level : UInt8)
    (maxOutputSize : Nat) (hsize : data.size < maxOutputSize) :
    Zip.Native.Inflate.inflate (deflateRaw data level) maxOutputSize = .ok data := by

Unified DEFLATE roundtrip: inflate ∘ deflateRaw = identity.

records.name: Zip.Native.Deflate.deflateRaw_pad
records.entry_name: lean-zip
records.statement:
theorem deflateRaw_pad (data : ByteArray) (level : UInt8) :
    ∃ (contentBits padding : List Bool),
      Deflate.Spec.bytesToBits (deflateRaw data level) = contentBits ++ padding ∧
      padding.length < 8 := by
  sorry
records.doc:
The output of `deflateRaw` decomposes into content bits plus short padding.
    Needed by `inflateRaw_endPos_ge` to establish that the native decoder
    consumes all of the deflated byte array.

records.name: Zip.Native.Deflate.deflateRaw_goR_pad
records.entry_name: lean-zip
records.statement:
theorem deflateRaw_goR_pad (data : ByteArray) (level : UInt8) :
    ∃ remaining,
      Deflate.Spec.decode.goR (Deflate.Spec.bytesToBits (deflateRaw data level)) []
        = some (data.data.toList, remaining) ∧ remaining.length < 8 := by
  sorry
records.doc:
For the encoder's output, `decode.goR` returns a short remaining (< 8 bits).
    Connects encoder structure to decoder bit consumption.

records.name: OneMfld.homeomorph_circle_or_unitInterval
records.entry_name: The classification of compact 1-manifolds
records.doc: A Lean 4 (mathlib) proof of the classification of 1-manifolds, specifically that every compact, connected, Hausdorff topological space charted on the half-line [0,∞) is homeomorphic to the circle S¹ or to the closed unit interval [0,1]. The proof follows David Gale's outline: shrink to a finite atlas of interval charts, then induct on the atlas size, merging two overlapping charts at each step; a connected overlap glues two charts into one (two boundary charts glue onto [0, 1]), while a disconnected overlap has exactly two components and yields the circle.
records.informal: Every compact connected Hausdorff space charted on the nonnegative real half-line is homeomorphic to the circle or the closed unit interval.

records.name: Distributed2Coloring.pStar_ge_23879
records.entry_name: 2-Coloring Cycles in One Round
records.doc: Formalizes certified upper and lower bounds for one-round randomized algorithms that 2-color cycles.
records.informal: Proves that every one-round classical algorithm has monochromatic-edge probability at least 0.23879.

records.name: ACMax.acmax_conjecture
records.entry_name: Kolokolnikov's ACMAX conjecture
records.doc: Proves that every simple graph on n ≥ 4 vertices with 2(n−2) edges has algebraic connectivity at most 2, attained by the complete bipartite graph K₂,ₙ₋₂. Develops Laplacian test-vector bounds, sparse cut certificates, and non-backtracking walk estimates used in the proof.

records.name: MooreBound.DegreeDiameter.theorem_1_1
records.entry_name: Asymptotically attaining the Moore bound
records.doc: Proves that, for each fixed positive diameter k, the largest order of a finite simple graph with maximum degree at most d and extended diameter at most k is asymptotic to d^k as d tends to infinity. Constructs regular halved-flag graphs over every finite field, with exact order and diameter, a sharp degree cap, and matching asymptotics through all prime powers. Also proves the corresponding lower-limit bound for the edge extremum defined using line-graph diameter. Reusable infrastructure includes common bases for complete flags, odd-even sorting routes, exact flag enumeration, projective-line completion counts, and bipartite graph expansion. The analytic bridge retains the Wiener-Ikehara and prime-counting dependency closure from the Apache-2.0 PrimeNumberTheoremAnd project. The paper describes AI-assisted formalization supervised by the human authors.
records.informal: For each positive natural k, n(k,d)/d^k tends to 1 as the natural degree bound d tends to infinity. Here n(k,d) is the maximum number of vertices of a finite simple graph with maximum degree at most d and extended diameter at most k.

records.name: LeanPool.AsymptoticTrianglePacking.trianglePackingGap
records.entry_name: Finite hypergraph rounding and the asymptotic triangle-packing gap
records.doc: Formalizes a finite ceiling-carrying nibble theorem for uniform hypergraphs that are near-regular outside a small exceptional set and have suitably bounded codegrees, and derives the uniform subquadratic gap between fractional and integral triangle packing in finite graphs, together with its fractional-cover formulation.

records.name: BannaiBannaiStanton.bannai_bannai_stanton_bound
records.entry_name: The Bannai-Bannai-Stanton Bound on Distance Sets
records.doc: Formalizes the Bannai-Bannai-Stanton theorem: a distance set `S` in `ℝ^d` realizing `s` distinct distances has size at most `Nat.choose (d + s) s`. Follows the short polynomial-method proof of Petrov and Pohoata via a generalized Croot-Lev-Pach rank lemma, with auxiliary results on the diagonal linear-independence argument for polynomials, monomial counting of bounded degree, and a rank bound for sums of matrices.
records.informal: A distance set `S` in Euclidean space `ℝ^d` realizing `s` distinct distances satisfies `S.encard ≤ Nat.choose (d + s) s`.

records.name: BeckFialaMatrix.exists_rounding
records.entry_name: Strict Beck–Fiala rounding for incidence matrices
records.doc: Proves the rational integer-making form of Beck–Fiala rounding for finite zero-one incidence matrices with column degree bounded by a positive t. Every row has discrepancy strictly less than t, and initially integral coordinates are preserved. Includes the necessity of the positive-bound hypothesis. This is distinct from the Komlós discrepancy bound and from the non-strict hyperedge-selection rounding used in triangle packing.
records.informal: Given a finite zero-one integer matrix with at most t ones per column, t at least one, and a rational vector in the unit cube, there is a zero-one integer vector whose discrepancy in every row is strictly less than t.

records.name: MeasurableSelection.exists_measurable_selection
records.entry_name: BicausalOT: measurable selection and coupling strategies
records.doc: Develops Kuratowski–Ryll-Nardzewski selection, Jankov–von Neumann uniformization, and finite-horizon Bellman identities for locally feasible coupling strategies. Exact Borel measurable optimal strategies and initial couplings are obtained on Polish Borel spaces for weakly continuous probability kernels and nonnegative extended-real lower semicontinuous costs. Equivalence with optimization over bicausal path laws is not established.
records.informal: A weakly measurable multifunction from an arbitrary measurable space to a Polish space with nonempty closed values admits an everywhere-defined Borel-measurable selector.

records.name: Biswal.Theorem23.thm_manifest_coeff_nonneg
records.entry_name: Chebyshev Quotients and Demazure Multiplicities
records.doc: Formalizes positivity results for the coefficients of Chebyshev-type polynomial quotients attached to integer partitions, modelling Demazure multiplicities. Proves that the relevant generating function is a polynomial and that its coefficients are eventually positive (Theorem 1), gives explicit Cauchy-product and matrix-inverse formulas for the coefficients (Theorem 2), and establishes their nonnegativity through a Dyck-path lattice counting model (Theorem 3).
records.informal: Proves that every coefficient of the generating function is nonnegative, via the explicit Dyck-path lattice counting model.

records.name: BSLambda.Final.exists_bs_gt_lam_rpow
records.entry_name: Block sensitivity can exceed spectral sensitivity squared
records.doc: Constructs a total Boolean function on 14011 blocks of 144 bits with block sensitivity at least 14011 and squared spectral sensitivity at most U = 7149 + 2 sqrt(150108). Proves the strict separation lambda(f)^2.12 < bs(f), multiplicativity of spectral sensitivity under arbitrary block composition, and an exponential lower bound with factor 14011/U > 1.768 for the self-composed family. Includes reusable finite product probability, an asymmetric Lovasz local lemma, partial Boolean assignments, certificate-family spectral bounds, and a Paley doubly regular tournament. The formalized explicit exponent is 2.12; the exact logarithmic exponent is also retained.
records.informal: There exists a total Boolean function on ZMod 14011 times Fin 144 whose block sensitivity strictly exceeds its spectral sensitivity raised to the real exponent 2.12.

records.name: BollobasNikiforov.lambda1_sq_add_lambda2_sq_le
records.entry_name: The Bollobás–Nikiforov conjecture
records.doc: Proves the Bollobás–Nikiforov conjecture (2007): every finite noncomplete simple graph G on at least two vertices satisfies λ₁(G)² + λ₂(G)² ≤ 2 (1 - 1/ω(G)) |E(G)|, where λ₁ ≥ λ₂ are the two largest adjacency eigenvalues and ω(G) is the clique number. The inequality is derived from a weighted spectral inequality for symmetric entrywise nonnegative matrices supported on the edges of G, which in turn rests on a complete positivity theorem for planar Gram matrices and a rank-two Gram inequality. The rank-two Gram inequality also identifies the conic parameter of Coutinho, Spier and Zhang with the clique number. The supporting library develops the completely positive cone and its closedness, the Motzkin–Straus inequality in completely positive form, total nonnegativity of truncated-square and convex kernels via Cauchy–Binet, weighted Laplacian updates, Schur complements, Perron eigenvectors, the Schur product theorem and Cauchy interlacing over Mathlib.
records.informal: For every finite simple graph G on at least two vertices that is not complete, the two largest adjacency eigenvalues satisfy λ₁(G)² + λ₂(G)² ≤ 2 (1 - 1/ω(G)) |E(G)|, with ω(G) the clique number and |E(G)| the number of edges.

records.name: BooleanIsoperimetry.harper_theorem
records.entry_name: Boolean Isoperimetry and Conway--Guy Coherent Gaps
records.doc: Formalizes Harper's vertex-isoperimetric theorem for the Boolean cube: among all families of a fixed cardinality, the simplicial initial segment has the smallest closed radius-one Hamming neighborhood. Develops the supporting binomial-cascade identities, Kruskal--Katona shadow bounds, coordinate compressions, and the final dimension induction. Applies the coherent-gap certificate method to prove normalized consecutive-gap rigidity for the Conway--Guy sequence from its exact recurrence.
records.informal: For every family of vertices in an n-dimensional Boolean cube, the simplicial initial segment of the same cardinality has a closed radius-one Hamming neighborhood no larger than that of the family.

records.name: UnrestrictedBooleanMul.N4.mc_mul_four
records.entry_name: Exact Boolean multiplicative complexity of four-term polynomial multiplication
records.doc: Proves that multiplying two binary polynomials with n coefficients needs exactly 0, 1, 3, 6, and 9 AND gates for n = 0, 1, 2, 3, and 4, with XOR and constants free and arbitrary reuse of earlier nonlinear wires. The main lower bound excludes every eight-gate circuit for n = 4. Develops Boolean algebraic normal forms equivalent to all Boolean functions, a general circuit model, dimension bounds, circuit rewiring, a Reed-Muller minimum-weight theorem, and exterior-algebra and jet arguments controlling nonlinear feedback.
records.informal: Multiplying two four-coefficient binary polynomials needs exactly nine AND gates, allowing free XOR, constants, and unrestricted nonlinear reuse.

records.name: MeasureTheory.Lp_Burkholder_inequality_martingaleTransform
records.entry_name: Burkholder Martingale Transform Inequality
records.doc: Formalizes Burkholder's sharp Lp inequality for real-valued martingale transforms: if `f` is a discrete martingale and `w` a predictable multiplier bounded by `1`, then the Lp norm of the transform `w ⋆ₘ f` is at most `(pStar p - 1)` times the Lp norm of `f`, where `pStar p` is the maximum of `p` and its conjugate exponent. The proof builds the Burkholder special function as a majorant of the relevant payoff in each exponent regime (`1 < p < 2`, `p = 2`, `p > 2`).
records.informal: The sharp Lp Burkholder inequality: for a discrete martingale `f` and a predictable multiplier `w` with `|w n| ≤ 1`, the Lp norm of the martingale transform `(w ⋆ₘ f) n` is bounded by `(pStar p - 1)` times the Lp norm of `f n`.

records.name: LeanPool.CenteredMaximal.ofReal_phi_le_weakTypeConstant_two
records.entry_name: Bounds for the centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal constant
records.doc: Proves that the weak type (1,1) constant c_2 of the centered maximal operator over axis-parallel squares is at least the explicit radical phi, approximately 1.68551, using a weighted periodic lattice and integrable approximations. Also proves c_d <= 2^d in every natural dimension and 1.685 < phi < 1.686. The operator acts on real-valued integrable functions, with Lebesgue outer measure of strict level sets. Includes the maximal-function API, a Vitali covering argument, lattice witnesses, smearing estimates, and the limiting lower bound. No optimality of phi is claimed.
records.informal: The explicit radical phi is a lower bound for c_2, the infimum of all weak type (1,1) bounds for the centered maximal operator over axis-parallel squares in the real plane.

records.name: Champernowne.champernowne_normal
records.entry_name: Champernowne normality in every base
records.doc: Proves that concatenating the base-b digits of the positive integers gives a normal digit sequence for every integer base b at least 2: every nonempty length-k word of digits below b has limiting frequency b^(-k). This is a discrete, all-base generalization of D. G. Champernowne's 1933 base-ten result, without a real-number expansion bridge. Includes reusable substring-counting inequalities, a digit-string equivalence, exact cohort counts, and quantitative prefix bounds used to establish the frequency limit.
records.informal: For every integer base b at least 2, the sequence formed by concatenating the base-b digits of 1, 2, 3, and so on is normal: each nonempty word w of digits below b has limiting occurrence frequency 1 / b^(length w), counting overlapping occurrences.

records.name: ChannelCapacity.exists_unique_capacity_achieving_prior_of_finite
records.entry_name: Uniqueness of Shannon Capacity-Achieving Priors
records.doc: Formalizes uniqueness of the capacity-achieving input distribution for a Markov-kernel channel in three aligned layers: a finite-alphabet theorem (compactness, continuity, and strict concavity of mutual information on Mathlib's weak topology for `ProbabilityMeasure`), a concrete discharged theorem for compact-Polish channels with a common strictly positive jointly continuous density, and a general measure-theoretic packaging that isolates the abstract well-conditioning hypotheses, plus a counterexample showing pairwise-distinct rows do not give an injective prior pushforward (the non-degeneracy required for uniqueness).
records.informal: For a Markov kernel between finite alphabets (nonempty input) whose rows are linearly independent (`Kernel.RowMatrixFullRank`), a capacity-achieving input prior exists and is unique.

records.informal: For compact-Polish channels with a common strictly positive jointly continuous density, given injectivity of the prior-pushforward map and upper semicontinuity of mutual information (the latter carried as a field of `Kernel.ContinuousPositiveDensity`, not derived), the capacity-achieving prior is unique.

records.name: ChipFiring.Propositions.riemann_roch
records.entry_name: Chip-Firing with Lean 4
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Baker and Norine's Riemann-Roch theorem for finite graphs. Chip configurations on a finite graph, modulo chip-firing moves, form an abelian group analogous to the group of line bundles on a compact Riemann surface. Each class can be assigned a rank, analogous to the dimension of a linear series. These ranks then satisfy a formula of the form r(D) - r(K-D) = deg D + 1 - g, in exact analogy to Riemann surfaces. This formula is formalized, along with the analog of Clifford's theorem for finite graphs.
records.informal: For a finite connected graph, the ranks of a divisor and its canonical complement satisfy the graph Riemann–Roch formula.

records.informal: For a special divisor on a finite connected graph, its rank is at most half its degree.

records.name: Chudnovsky.chudnovskySum_eq_pi_inv
records.entry_name: A Detailed Proof of the Chudnovsky Formula
records.doc: Formalizes the Chudnovsky brothers' rapidly convergent series for 1/π, proving Mathlib's `chudnovskySum = π⁻¹`. Follows Milla's elementary complex-analytic proof: Weierstrass and Eisenstein theory, Liouville and parallelogram-residue calculus, the Kummer hypergeometric bridge and the main modular identity relating the j-invariant to the lattice periods, Baker's division-value machinery, and the singular-moduli inputs at the CM point τ = (1 + √-163)/2 — integrality of j(τ) via modular polynomials and Kronecker's congruence, and rationality of the Weierstrass s₂ invariant via Masser's Appendix A.1.
records.informal: Proves the Chudnovsky series identity, i.e. Mathlib's `chudnovskySum = π⁻¹`: the series (12 / 640320^(3/2)) · ∑ₙ (-1)ⁿ (6n)! (545140134 n + 13591409) / ((3n)! (n!)³ 640320^(3n)) sums to 1/π.

records.name: Chvatal.chvatal
records.entry_name: Chvátal's conjecture and sharp Boolean correlation
records.doc: Formalizes Chang, Liu, and Liu's proof that a hereditary family on a finite nonempty ground set has a largest intersecting subfamily that is a star. Develops the sharp Boolean Fourier correlation inequality, its antipodal and quadratic forms, sharpness examples, and the weighted star theorem for nonnegative decreasing weights.
records.informal: Every intersecting subfamily A of a hereditary finite family D on a finite nonempty ground type has cardinality at most that of some star of D.

records.name: SaxlCounterexamples.MainTheorems.mainTheorem
records.entry_name: Common-neighbour counterexamples for Saxl graphs
records.doc: Proves that for every base size B at least two and every prescribed degree bound, there is a finite faithful primitive permutation group of at least that degree and exact base size B whose generalized Saxl graph contains two nonadjacent vertices with no common neighbor. records.informal: For every natural number B at least two and every degree bound, there exists a finite faithful primitive permutation group of degree at least the bound and base size exactly B whose generalized Saxl graph has two nonadjacent vertices with no common neighbor.

records.name: CompactSelfAdjoint.exists_hasEigenvector_iSup_or_iInf_of_isCompactOperator
records.entry_name: Spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators
records.doc: Formalizes the spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators on a Hilbert space: such an operator admits a Hilbert basis of eigenvectors. The development passes from weak compactness of Hilbert closed balls and Rayleigh-quotient extrema to an eigenvector at the operator norm, finiteness of the point spectrum outside any neighbourhood of zero, finite-rank cutoff approximation, and finally the orthogonal decomposition into eigenspaces.
records.informal: A compact self-adjoint operator has an eigenvector whose eigenvalue realizes either the supremum or the infimum of its Rayleigh quotient.

records.name: CompactnessConjecture.quantitativeCompactnessCounterexample
records.entry_name: Counterexamples to graph compactness and two-degenerate extremal bounds
records.doc: Formalizes two counterexamples in extremal graph theory. The first gives a finite family of connected bipartite cyclic graphs whose family extremal number grows strictly slower than every member's extremal number, disproving the Erdős--Simonovits compactness conjecture. The second constructs a connected bipartite two-degenerate graph with extremal number at least c n^(3/2+ε), disproving the proposed universal n^(3/2) upper bound under the stated bipartition degree condition.
records.informal: There is a nonempty finite family of connected bipartite cyclic graphs such that every member has a uniform positive n^(4/3)-scale extremal lower bound, while every family-free host on n vertices has its sixteenth power of the edge count bounded by a constant times n^21. Consequently the family is not compact and the Erdős--Simonovits compactness conjecture is false.

records.entry_name: Counterexamples to graph compactness and two-degenerate extremal bounds
records.doc: Formalizes two counterexamples in extremal graph theory. The first gives a finite family of connected bipartite cyclic graphs whose family extremal number grows strictly slower than every member's extremal number, disproving the Erdős--Simonovits compactness conjecture. The second constructs a connected bipartite two-degenerate graph with extremal number at least c n^(3/2+ε), disproving the proposed universal n^(3/2) upper bound under the stated bipartition degree condition.
records.informal: There is a connected bipartite two-degenerate finite graph H such that each side of every two-coloring has a vertex of degree greater than two, yet ex(n,H) is eventually at least c n^(3/2+ε) for some positive constants c and ε.

records.name: CompositionAlgebra.hurwitz_classification
records.entry_name: Hurwitz's Classification of Euclidean Composition Algebras
records.doc: Formalizes Hurwitz's classification of nontrivial finite-dimensional real Euclidean composition algebras: every such algebra has dimension 1, 2, 4, or 8 and is real-linearly equivalent to the real numbers, complex numbers, quaternions, or octonions through a map preserving the unit, multiplication, and norm form. The development also constructs the octonions from an explicit Fano multiplication table, proves Degen's eight-square identity, and shows that Cayley--Dickson doubling preserves the composition law for associative inputs.
records.informal: Every nontrivial finite-dimensional real Euclidean composition algebra is linearly equivalent to the real numbers, complex numbers, quaternions, or octonions through a map preserving the unit, multiplication, and norm form.

records.name: CutAndProject.main_theorem_geometric_concrete
records.entry_name: Period Lengths of Rational Cut-and-Project Gap Sequences
records.doc: Formalizes the closed-form minimal periods of one-dimensional rational cut-and-project gap sequences at the level of the paper's residue model, plus a fully geometric aperiodicity theorem for irrational slopes. For coprime α, β ∈ ℕ and window parameter ω ≥ 0, write N = ⌊ωα⌋ + ⌊ωβ⌋ + 1 and D = α² + β². The strip-to-residue reduction of the paper — sorting the hits of the length-N progression twisted by the geometric multiplier −αβ⁻¹ (mod D) — is taken as the definition of the gap sequence rather than derived from the lattice; for it, the multiset convention has minimal period N/D when D ∣ N and N otherwise, and the set convention (multiplicities flattened to {0,1}) has minimal period 1 when N ≥ D and N otherwise. The irrational case is geometric from first principles: for positive irrational slope and ω > 0, the accepted points of ℤ² sorted by the physical projection have a gap sequence with no finite period, via injectivity of the projection and Kronecker density of the internal image.
records.informal: The gap sequence of the residue model of the rational cut-and-project multiset (sorted hits of the length-N progression under the multiplier −αβ⁻¹ mod D) has minimal period N/D if D divides N and N otherwise, where N = ⌊ωα⌋ + ⌊ωβ⌋ + 1 and D = α² + β².

records.name: Combinatorics.Line.exists_of_density_atTop
records.entry_name: The density Hales–Jewett theorem and Szemerédi's theorem
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the density Hales–Jewett theorem: for every finite alphabet α and every density δ > 0, all sufficiently large n have the property that any set of at least δ·|α|^n words of length n over α contains a combinatorial line. The basis for the formalization is the combinatorial proof of Dodos, Kanellopoulos, and Tyros. As a consequence, we also formalize Szemerédi's theorem on the integers: for every k ≥ 3 and δ > 0, the following holds for all sufficiently large n. Any subset of {0, …, n−1} of size at least δ·n contains a nonconstant arithmetic progression of length k.
records.informal: Every positive-density subset of sufficiently long words over a finite nontrivial alphabet contains a combinatorial line.

records.name: CategoryTheory.Dilatations.Dila_universal_property
records.entry_name: Dilatations of categories and commutative rings
records.doc: Constructs categorical dilatations from sieves of permitted numerators and denominator morphisms, and proves their universal property for Sigma-regular functors satisfying the sieve containment condition. Develops restriction and union of centers, dual codilatations, and ordinary localization as a special case. The composition isomorphism retains the explicit Sigma-regularity hypothesis left open in the original paper. For commutative rings, an exponent-profile center recovers the ring dilatation; the naive single-index comparison is refuted over Z[X]. A finite category example refutes a general intermediate-category characterization. Independent ring modules provide fraction arithmetic, a universal property, reindexing, and the unique isomorphism for two-stage dilatations.
records.informal: For a nonempty indexed center in a category C and a functor F from C to D, assume that localization of D at the images of the chosen denominators is faithful and that each pushed-forward numerator sieve lies in the sieve generated by its mapped denominator. There is a unique functor from the dilatation to D whose composite with the canonical functor from C is F.

records.name: DistanceGeometry.schoenberg
records.entry_name: Euclidean Distance Geometry
records.doc: Develops the basepoint-centered Gram approach to finite Euclidean distance geometry. Proves both directions of Schoenberg's characterization, including a rank-controlled factorization of positive-semidefinite matrices; proves that three affinely independent centers in Euclidean three-space determine at most two points with prescribed distances; and verifies the Cayley--Menger determinant for segments and triangles, including the triangle-area identity underlying Heron's formula.
records.informal: For n at least one, a symmetric hollow n-by-n matrix is a squared-distance matrix of points in k-dimensional Euclidean space exactly when its basepoint-centered Gram matrix is positive semidefinite and has rank at most k.

records.name: Egrs75.MuFinish.egrs_two_prime_mu
records.entry_name: The Erdős–Graham–Ruzsa–Straus two-prime theorem
records.doc: A complete machine-checked proof that for any two distinct odd primes p and q there are infinitely many n with binom(2n,n) coprime to pq, including the iterated carry-controlled digit-clearing step that Bloom and Croot defer to the 1975 paper, via a per-move lexicographic measure, an elementary staircase lemma, and a Dirichlet-approximation seed.
records.informal: Proves that for distinct odd primes p and q there are infinitely many n with p and q both not dividing the central binomial coefficient binom(2n,n), via the mu-measure descent.

records.name: Ehrhart.Volume.ehrhart_volume_inequality_for_sets
records.entry_name: Ehrhart's sharp volume inequality
records.doc: Proves Ehrhart's sharp upper bound for the volume of a centered full-dimensional convex body whose origin is its unique interior lattice point. The development builds the weighted complex-analytic and variational machinery needed for the bound and verifies sharpness using the centered simplex, including its barycenter and exact volume.
records.informal: In every positive dimension, a compact full-dimensional convex set with barycenter zero and origin as its unique interior lattice point has volume at most (n + 1)^n / n!.

records.name: EllipticPdes.Regularity.higher_interior_regularity
records.entry_name: Linear elliptic PDE: solvability, regularity and spectral theory

records.name: Erdos97Octagon.erdos97_convex_octagon
records.entry_name: The Convex-Octagon Case of Erdős Problem 97
records.doc: Proves that among eight labelled points in the Euclidean plane in convex position, at least one point has no four other points at a common distance. The development reduces a geometric counterexample to a finite incidence model, classifies normalized row patterns up to symmetry, proves geometric and algebraic obstructions, and excludes seven canonical first-row masks with a kernel-audited exhaustive search over the remaining legal row masks and checked geometric obstruction witnesses. This is the modern four-equidistant formulation; Erdős's 1946 paper posed the stronger three-equidistant version. This is the convex-octagon case only; the general Erdős Problem 97 remains open.

records.name: LeanPool.ErdosMoser.leoMoserVarianceBound
records.entry_name: Leo Moser's finite distinct-subset-sums inequality
records.doc: Formalizes the exact finite sum-of-squares inequality that Guy's 1982 account states as Theorem 2 and attributes to Leo Moser: a finite set A of natural numbers with distinct subset sums satisfies 4^|A| - 1 <= 3 * sum(a^2). It then derives direct and square-root lower bounds for the largest element of A. This does not claim the stronger historical asymptotic bound attributed jointly to Erdős and Moser, and Erdős Problem 1 remains open.
records.informal: If a finite set A of natural numbers has distinct subset sums, then 4^|A| - 1 is at most three times the sum of the squares of the elements of A.

records.name: LeanPool.Erdos132ConvexK3.convex_top_three_degree_six
records.entry_name: Convex Three-Distance Degree-Six Theorem and Exceptional-Word Closures
records.doc: Proves that every finite cyclically strictly convex planar configuration has a vertex incident to at most six edges from its three largest distance classes. The proof selects a maximal-gap vertex and coordinated majorants, closes all exceptional inner branches, performs the five-row enumeration, and transports all thirteen canonical cover words to four shared full-two-rung, anti-saturation, terminal-cage, and four-edge-cage predicates. It also proves exceptional-count rigidity and an explicit heptagon refutation of a tempting stronger majorant claim, with rational regression witnesses. This settles the all-n k=3 instance of the paper's suggested degree-2k convex bound; Morić--Pritchard proved the corresponding top-three edge bound for sufficiently large n. It does not settle the general-k suggestion or the general Erdős problem 132.
records.informal: For every nonempty finite cyclically strictly convex planar configuration with three strictly ordered largest squared-distance classes d₁, d₂, and d₃, some vertex is incident to at most six pairs whose squared distance is one of those three classes.

records.name: Erdos132ThreeChain.nonDiameterSqDists_ne_chain
records.entry_name: Planar Point Sets Whose Non-Diameter Distances Form a Geometric 3-Chain
records.doc:
Formalizes a support theorem about planar point sets whose non-diameter squared distances are confined to a geometric progression of ratio three. The chain-quadruple theorem shows that no planar quadruple with all six squared distances in such a chain can span two chain steps, and classifies the seven labelled patterns that do occur: the rhombus of two glued equilateral triangles, in five positions of its long edge, and the equilateral triangle with its centroid, in two. A Gram obstruction then rules out any five-point chain configuration. The lift to n at least thirteen runs through the diameter graph: the Caro--Wei independence bound, proved here, produces an independent five-set once the diameter graph is known to have at most as many edges as the set has points. That edge bound is the Hopf--Pannwitz theorem of 1934, and it already exists in the pool; this project reproves it in its own model as a supporting lemma, claiming no novelty for it, and the overlap is set out in full below. The result is unconditional.
There is no prior write-up behind this development. The restriction to ratio 3 is ad hoc: the 3-chain statement was produced by the author's automated research pipeline in August 2026, while the cited source poses the ambient Erdos problem and does not state this restriction or result. This theorem does not resolve Erdos 132, whose distance spectra need not be geometric 3-chains. The descriptive labels used in the Lean docstrings are internal to this development and refer to no numbered result elsewhere.
Overlap disclosure. Erdos132ThreeChain.hopfPannwitz is NOT offered as a new result. The pooled project Erdos132N14 already contains the same diameter bound, and the version here exists only so that this project is self-contained. Its statement, verbatim from LeanPool/Erdos132N14/HopfPannwitz.lean, is

    theorem diameterEdges_card_le
        (P : Configuration ι) (S : Finset ι) {d : ℝ}
        (hd : 0 < d)
        (hmax : ∀ f ∈ pairs S, P.pairDistance f ≤ d) :
        (diameterEdges P S d).card ≤ S.card

where, from LeanPool/Erdos132N14/Basic.lean, `Configuration ι` is a structure carrying an injective `point : ι → ℂ`, `pairs S = (S ×ˢ S).filter fun e ↦ e.1 < e.2` for a `LinearOrder ι`, `pairDistance P e = dist (P.point e.1) (P.point e.2)`, and `diameterEdges P S d = (pairs S).filter fun e ↦ P.pairDistance e = d`. The corresponding statement here is

    theorem hopfPannwitz {X : Finset Point} {D : ℝ} (hD : IsSqDiameter X D) :
        ∑ v ∈ X, degree (DiameterAdj D) X v ≤ 2 * X.card

with `Point = ℝ × ℝ`, `sqDist` the squared Euclidean distance, `DiameterAdj D p q = (p ≠ q ∧ sqDist p q = D)`, `degree adj X v = (X.filter (adj v)).card`, and `IsSqDiameter X D` asserting that `D` is realised by two distinct points of `X` and dominates every squared distance inside `X`. The two are the same mathematical theorem — a positive maximal distance is realised at most as often as there are points — carried by different models: an injective map from a linearly ordered index type into the complex plane, counting a Finset of unordered pairs, against a Finset of points of the real plane, in squared distances and degree-sum form. Neither statement is an instance of the other without a model bridge: a LinearOrder on ℝ × ℝ, a dist-to-sqDist transfer, and a handshake lemma. The proofs differ too, Perles charging there against pendant deletion driven by Cramer's rule here. No project in the pool imports another, and CONTRIBUTING.md records that independence as the property the fast per-project build relies on, so this project reproves the bound rather than importing it. It is a supporting lemma of this development, not one of its results, and it is therefore not listed among the main results below.
Two supporting identities also exist elsewhere in the pool. From LeanPool/Erdos97ConvexOctagon/CayleyMenger.lean,

    theorem cm4_sqDist_eq_zero (a b c d : Plane) :
        cm4 (sqDist a b) (sqDist a c) (sqDist a d)
          (sqDist b c) (sqDist b d) (sqDist c d) = 0

over `Plane = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)` is the same four-point Cayley--Menger vanishing as this project's

    theorem gramDet_eq_zero (a b c d : Point) :
        gramDet (sqDist a b) (sqDist a c) (sqDist a d) (sqDist b c) (sqDist b d) (sqDist c d) = 0

over `Point = ℝ × ℝ`; both are one-line `ring` identities in the coordinates. From LeanPool/DistanceGeometry/SchoenbergHard.lean,

    theorem schoenberg {D : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ} (hD : IsPreDistMatrix D) :
        EmbedsIn D k ↔ (centeredGram D).PosSemidef ∧ (centeredGram D).rank ≤ k

characterizes Euclidean distance matrices in general dimension. This project never invokes it: the four-point condition is used directly as a `ring` identity and the five-point obstruction is a sum-of-squares contradiction, so no positive-semidefiniteness criterion is needed.
records.informal: Let n be at least thirteen, let a be positive, and let X be a finite set of points of the real plane with exactly n elements. Suppose D is the squared diameter of X, meaning that D is realised by two distinct points of X and dominates every squared distance inside X. Then for every natural number h, the set of squared distances realised by distinct points of X and different from D is not equal to the geometric 3-chain consisting of a times 3^j for j below h.

records.name: Erdos137.erdos137_finite
records.entry_name: Erdős Problem #137: powerful products of consecutive integers
records.doc: Formalizes the abc-conditional finiteness results for Erdős Problem #137 (Erdős–Selfridge): a number N is powerful if every prime dividing N has its square dividing N, and the question is whether the product F(k,n) = n(n+1)⋯(n+k-1) of k ≥ 3 consecutive integers can be powerful for infinitely many n. Each route isolates its abc input (a radical lower bound) as a single explicit hypothesis and proves everything else outright, concluding that, conditionally, F(k,n) is powerful for only finitely many n for each fixed k ≥ 3.
records.informal: Under the Granville–Langevin radical bound RadLB k (an abc-conditional hypothesis) and k ≥ 3, the set of n ≥ 1 for which F(k,n) is powerful is finite.

records.name: Erdos346.intended_problem_if_limit_exists
records.entry_name: Erdős Problem 346: Ratio Limit Forces the Golden Ratio
records.doc: Formalizes the limit-exists interpretation of Erdős Problem 346: for a strictly increasing positive integer sequence with a uniform ratio gap whose finite deletions are complete but whose infinite deletions are not, if the consecutive quotient sequence converges to some real limit greater than one, then that limit must equal the golden ratio and the quotient sequence tends to it.
records.informal: Existence of any limit greater than one for the quotient sequence forces convergence to the golden ratio, the intended Erdős–Graham conclusion.

records.name: Erdos548.erdos_548
records.entry_name: The Erdős–Sós conjecture (Erdős Problem 548)
records.doc: Proves the Erdős–Sós conjecture (1962), Erdős Problem 548: every graph on n ≥ k+1 vertices with at least (k−1)n/2 + 1 edges contains every tree on k+1 vertices as a (not necessarily induced) subgraph. The headline statement is the FrontierMath Erdős benchmark statement, reviewed by Thomas Bloom and carried verbatim by Google DeepMind's Formal Conjectures; the proof was found autonomously by GPT-6 Astra. It is a finite double counting over permutation words of the host vertices: rotating the first qualifying prefix of a cut word gives a gluing inequality for two rooted branches, and reversing the two blocks of a cut moves the root to a newly attached leaf. A strong induction on the order t of the tree bounds the adjacency-marked cut words by the rooted-copy count plus (t−2)·n!, so a tree-free host on n vertices has at most (t−2)n/2 edges, the sharp classical bound.
records.informal: Let n ≥ k+1. Every simple graph on n vertices with at least (k−1)n/2 + 1 edges contains every tree on k+1 vertices as a subgraph (an injective graph homomorphism). This is Erdős Problem 548, the Erdős–Sós conjecture, in the benchmark phrasing.

records.name: Erdos865.erdos865_upper_bound
records.entry_name: A sharp 5/8 bound for Erdős Problem 865
records.doc: Formalizes the resolution of Erdős Problem 865 on pairwise sums. For A ⊆ {1,…,N}, a pairwise-sum triple is a set of distinct a, b, c ∈ A with a+b, a+c, b+c all in A, and A is triple-free when it has none. The development proves that every triple-free A ⊆ [1,N] satisfies 8·|A| ≤ 5·N + 53, that any A exceeding this bound contains a triple, and — via the construction A = [M,2M] ∪ [4M,8M] for N = 8M — that the constant 5/8 is optimal, so f₃(N) = 5N/8 + O(1). The upper bound runs through a folded additive lemma over ℤ/mℤ (a four-set union bound) and a folding lemma, closed by strong induction on N.
records.informal: Every triple-free set A ⊆ [1,N] satisfies 8·|A| ≤ 5·N + 53, i.e. |A| ≤ (5/8)·N + O(1).

records.name: Erdos865.sharpness
records.entry_name: A sharp 5/8 bound for Erdős Problem 865
records.doc: Formalizes the resolution of Erdős Problem 865 on pairwise sums. For A ⊆ {1,…,N}, a pairwise-sum triple is a set of distinct a, b, c ∈ A with a+b, a+c, b+c all in A, and A is triple-free when it has none. The development proves that every triple-free A ⊆ [1,N] satisfies 8·|A| ≤ 5·N + 53, that any A exceeding this bound contains a triple, and — via the construction A = [M,2M] ∪ [4M,8M] for N = 8M — that the constant 5/8 is optimal, so f₃(N) = 5N/8 + O(1). The upper bound runs through a folded additive lemma over ℤ/mℤ (a four-set union bound) and a folding lemma, closed by strong induction on N.
records.informal: For N = 8M with M ≥ 1 there is a triple-free A ⊆ [1,N] with 8·|A| = 5·N + 16, so the constant 5/8 is optimal.

records.name: EuclideanJordan.frameBlock_isInternal
records.entry_name: Euclidean Jordan algebras and the frame Peirce decomposition
records.doc: The frame Peirce decomposition: relative to a Jordan frame, a Euclidean Jordan algebra is the internal direct sum of the blocks V_ij over unordered pairs of frame indices, and in finite dimension the diagonal blocks are lines, dim V_ii = 1 - the Faraut-Koranyi table entry. The frame is carried as data, so frame conjugacy is sidestepped and nothing here claims anything about the rank of J. Machine checked, not peer reviewed, no priority claim.
records.informal: A Euclidean Jordan algebra is the internal direct sum of the Peirce blocks associated with a Jordan frame.

records.name: ExpChaotic.devaney_chaotic
records.entry_name: Chaos and the Julia set of the complex exponential
records.doc: Formalizes the dynamics of z ↦ exp(z): escaping points, points with dense forward orbit, and repelling periodic points are dense in the complex plane; the map is chaotic in Devaney's sense and its Julia set is the whole plane. The development proves eventual covering of every compact set omitting zero, constructs contracting inverse branches, and rules out every locally uniform spherical subsequential limit on nonempty open sets. It includes general normal-sequence restriction lemmas, quantitative open mapping, and a two-target obstruction for arbitrary separated uniform codomains. The Lean proofs were primarily generated by AI under Lasse Rempe's direction. The initial six-lemma architecture adapts John Harrison's HOL Light formalization, credited with its retained BSD notice in the entry module.
records.informal: The complex exponential is continuous, has dense periodic points, and the monoid action generated by its iterates is topologically transitive on the complex plane.

records.name: Feige.sharp_unit_slack_feige_complete
records.entry_name: Feige's sharp unit-slack inequality
records.doc: For small-universe probability spaces, proves the sharp fixed-dimensional unit-slack lower bound for sums of independent nonnegative random variables: if each coordinate has mean at most one, then the probability that the sum lies below its mean plus one is at least (n/(n+1))^n, and this constant is optimal. The supporting library formalizes the Vlassis--Thomas exact distribution-free calibration theorem, Grünbaum's centroid-halfspace inequality and sharp simplex example, and the normalized-exponential bridge joining them.
records.informal: For every positive dimension n and every small-universe probability space, the sharp fixed-dimensional lower bound for the strict event that a sum of independent nonnegative random variables is below its expectation plus one is (n/(n+1))^n, and an explicit finite family proves optimality.

records.name: FiniteGraphFreeGroup.graphTopologicalFundamentalGroupEquiv
records.entry_name: Fundamental groups of finite connected graphs
records.doc: Constructs the standard interval-cell realization of a finite connected directed multigraph and proves that its topological fundamental group is a free group of rank E - V + 1. The proof uses an explicit spanning-tree basis and develops a verified path-lifting cover, a contraction of the covering tree, root-change equivalences, the tree/triviality criterion, and the corresponding free-abelian result.
records.informal: For a finite weakly connected directed multigraph, the topological fundamental group of its interval-cell quotient realization at any vertex is explicitly isomorphic to the free group on E + 1 - V generators.

records.name: GapCVP.Comparator.gapCVP400IsNPHard
records.entry_name: Polynomial-factor hardness of the closest vector problem
records.doc: Formalizes polynomial-factor NP-hardness of the closest vector problem through an explicit reduction from 3-SAT. The development also derives NP-hardness of binary nearest codeword, binary syndrome decoding, and finite p-norm variants of GapCVP. It includes machine-level polynomial-time bounds, binary encodings, affine systems, Reed--Solomon-style interpolation, and the lattice and coding-theory reductions needed by the final results.
records.informal: GapCVP in the Euclidean norm with approximation factor n^(1/400), where n is the lattice dimension, is NP-hard as a promise problem: every NP language reduces in polynomial time to the promise problem on encoded well-formed instances (positive dimension, nonsingular integer basis, positive rational radius) with an integer target, whose YES instances have a lattice vector within the radius of the target and whose NO instances have every lattice vector at distance greater than n^(1/400) times the radius.

records.name: GKPCarry.tendsto_gkpSuccessProportion_one
records.entry_name: Density-One GKP Divisibility and Its Carry-Language Characterization
records.doc: Proves that the exponents k satisfying the Graham--Knuth--Patashnik divisibility condition have natural density one. The proof gives an exact all-depth modular sieve, quantitative bounds for possible failures in initial intervals, and a density-zero limit for the failure proportion. It also develops the Kummer digit-sum bridge, the binary-popcount reduction, and a verified ternary carry automaton. The universal GKP conjecture remains open because the possible density-zero failure set may be nonempty.
records.informal: The proportion of exponents k below N for which nine divides the central binomial coefficient indexed by 2^k tends to one as N tends to infinity.

records.name: GoemansFlow.goemans_cost_conjecture_false
records.entry_name: Counterexample to Goemans' unsplittable-flow cost conjecture
records.doc: Refutes Goemans' cost conjecture for single-source unsplittable flow, Conjecture 1.3 of Traub, Vargas Koch, and Zenklusen's paper. A simple, loopless, acyclic graph with seven vertices and nine arcs admits a splittable flow of cost 58, but every unsplittable routing within the additive maximum-demand capacity bound costs at least 60, attained by an explicit routing. The development proves completeness of the walk enumeration and transfers the refutation from integers to any linearly ordered commutative ring, including the rationals and reals. Jason Hickey directed Claude's formal verification of the counterexample discovered by Dmitry Rybin with GPT-5.6 Pro; upstream also acknowledges Katherine Schlitz. Planarity is not part of the formalized claim.
records.informal: The rational form of Goemans' cost conjecture is false, even for simple, loopless, acyclic finite digraphs with explicit capacities, positive demands, and distinct terminals different from the source.

records.name: GoemansFlow.fractional_cost
records.entry_name: Counterexample to Goemans' unsplittable-flow cost conjecture
records.doc: Refutes Goemans' cost conjecture for single-source unsplittable flow, Conjecture 1.3 of Traub, Vargas Koch, and Zenklusen's paper. A simple, loopless, acyclic graph with seven vertices and nine arcs admits a splittable flow of cost 58, but every unsplittable routing within the additive maximum-demand capacity bound costs at least 60, attained by an explicit routing. The development proves completeness of the walk enumeration and transfers the refutation from integers to any linearly ordered commutative ring, including the rationals and reals. Jason Hickey directed Claude's formal verification of the counterexample discovered by Dmitry Rybin with GPT-5.6 Pro; upstream also acknowledges Katherine Schlitz. Planarity is not part of the formalized claim.
records.informal: The given splittable flow on the counterexample instance costs exactly 58.

records.name: GranvilleMoore.not_pow_succ_dvd_det_mooreMatrix_iff
records.entry_name: Integer Moore determinants and iterated Fermat quotients
records.doc: Proves Granville's integrality and congruence formulas for iterated Fermat quotients at odd primes, including the exceptional order p - 1. For 1 ≤ d ≤ p and integers x_j prime to p, it proves that the nonzero integer Moore determinant det(x_j^(p^i)) is divisible by p^C(d+1,3), and that the next power does not divide it exactly when the Fermat quotients q_p(x_j) are pairwise distinct modulo p. The development supplies polynomial coefficient identities, denominator-clearing and valuation estimates, a determinant reduction ladder, and weighted Vandermonde formulas over general commutative rings.
records.informal: Under those determinant hypotheses, its p-adic valuation is exactly C(d+1,3) if and only if the integer Fermat quotients q_p(x_j) have pairwise distinct residues modulo p. The Lean statement expresses exactness as failure of divisibility by p^(C(d+1,3)+1).

records.name: HadwigerNelsonBounds.hadwiger_nelson_known_bounds
records.entry_name: Known Bounds for the Hadwiger-Nelson Problem
records.doc: Formalizes the currently known bounds 5 <= chi(R^2) <= 7 for the chromatic number of the Euclidean plane. The upper bound constructs an explicit Isbell-style seven-coloring. The lower bound checks Parts' 481-vertex coloring certificate, develops a finite doubled triangular-lattice forcing gadget, proves its exact Euclidean embedding, and closes the four-color contradiction with a spindle construction. The exact chromatic number remains open.
records.informal: The chromatic number of the unit-distance graph on the Euclidean plane lies between five and seven, inclusive.

records.name: LeanPool.HansonWright.hanson_wright_inequality_hdp
records.entry_name: The Hanson-Wright inequality for sub-Gaussian quadratic forms
records.doc: Proves the finite-dimensional Hanson-Wright concentration inequality for quadratic forms of independent mean-zero sub-Gaussian real random variables whose maximum least global-MGF sub-Gaussian scale is positive, for matrices with positive Frobenius and operator norms. The bound uses the fixed universal coefficient 1 / (256 * exp(1)^2). This is the MGF normalization of the usual result; no formal identification with an Orlicz psi-2 norm is claimed. The development derives the required moment-generating-function certificate instead of assuming it, and contributes reusable scalar Bernstein, Chernoff, cumulant, sub-Gaussian-process, and finite-maximum infrastructure.
records.informal: For independent mean-zero real random variables with finite least global-MGF sub-Gaussian scales and positive maximum coordinate MGF scale, and a matrix with positive Frobenius and operator norms, the centered quadratic form satisfies the Hanson-Wright two-regime exponential tail bound with the fixed universal coefficient 1 / (256 * exp(1)^2).

records.name: HasseMinkowski.hasseMinkowski
records.entry_name: The Hasse–Minkowski theorem over ℚ
records.doc: Proves the local–global principle for quadratic forms over the rationals: a form is isotropic over ℚ exactly when it is isotropic over ℝ and over every p-adic completion, together with Meyer's theorem that an indefinite rational form in at least five variables is isotropic. The development builds the Hilbert symbol at every place of ℚ with Serre's explicit formulas (including the 2-adic case), proves Hilbert reciprocity and the existence theorem for prescribed local symbols, the Hasse invariant and the rank-two and rank-three local representability criteria, Legendre's ternary descent, and the rank-four and rank-≥5 inductions.
records.informal: A quadratic form over ℚ is isotropic if and only if it is isotropic over ℝ and over every p-adic completion ℚ_[p] (the Hasse–Minkowski local–global principle, in isotropy form).

records.informal: Every indefinite quadratic form over ℚ in at least five variables is isotropic (Meyer's theorem).

records.name: Mathoverflow1973.mathoverflow_1973
records.entry_name: A complex structure on the six-sphere
records.doc: Formalizes Levent Alpöge's construction of a complex-analytic atlas on the standard six-sphere. The development builds a compact complex threefold from torus fibrations with cusp and elliptic fibres, computes its homology and fundamental group, proves that its underlying topological space is homeomorphic to the six-sphere, and transports the complex atlas across that homeomorphism. It adapts Lean developments by Yury G. Kudryashov and Sebastian Kumar, together with the statement from the Formal Conjectures Authors.
records.informal: The formalized statement of MathOverflow question 1973: the standard six-sphere carries a complex three-dimensional manifold atlas.

records.name: PalomarHS.main_result
records.entry_name: Hard-sphere Mayer NBC identity and fork-packing volume bound
records.doc: A kernel-checked Lean formalization of the exact no-broken-circuit volume identity for hard-sphere Mayer cluster integrals and the stronger dimension-three fork-packing upper bound for each tree-owned NBC region. The development proves finite broken-circuit cancellation, the measurable finite-region decomposition, the anchored Euclidean product-measure theorem, and its explicit flat-coordinate transport.  Its geometric result is the attachment-aware estimate Vol(NBC_T) <= (17/32)^hardSphereNu T * hardSphereKappa^(k-1), where hardSphereNu T is the maximum cardinality of a packing of pairwise vertex-disjoint, order-compatible forks in T.  A formal fork is an ordered triple (a,b,c) with a < b < c, center a, leaves b,c, and tree edges {a,b} and {a,c}.  The central contribution is the complete pointwise-to-integral bridge together with the orientation-aware measure-preserving factorization that realizes the per-fork volume suppression.
records.informal: The absolute hard-sphere Mayer coefficient, multiplied by the factorial, equals the sum of nonnegative no-broken-circuit region volumes over spanning trees.

records.name: genus_eq_zero_iff_homeo
records.entry_name: The Jacobian of a Compact Riemann Surface
records.doc: Constructs the Jacobian of a compact Riemann surface as the period-lattice quotient of the dual of holomorphic 1-forms, and proves the surrounding theory it needs: the genus as the dimension of the space of holomorphic 1-forms, discreteness and full rank 2g of the period lattice, the Abel-Jacobi map and its injectivity in positive genus, functoriality (pushforward, pullback, degree, and the projection formula), Riemann-Roch, Serre duality via Laurent tails, the residue theorem, the Dolbeault-Cech comparison, and finite dimensionality of the first cohomology by a Schwartz/Montel argument. The headline no-hack guard is that the genus vanishes exactly when the surface is homeomorphic to the sphere.
records.informal: A compact connected Riemann surface has genus zero if and only if it is homeomorphic to the 2-sphere.

records.name: JL.johnson_lindenstrauss
records.entry_name: The Johnson–Lindenstrauss Lemma and Quantized JL
records.doc: Formalizes the Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma end to end — a Gaussian random projection preserves pairwise distances of a finite point set up to a (1 ± ε) factor, so a distortion-ε embedding of any m-point set exists once k is logarithmic in m — together with the quantized JL (QJL) one-bit sign sketch: unbiasedness of the asymmetric 1-bit estimator and its sub-Gaussian distortion bound.
records.informal: The abstract probabilistic-method union bound — if the summed per-pair distortion-failure probability is below one, a distortion-preserving map exists.

records.name: KahnKalai.covering_theorem
records.entry_name: Kahn–Kalai expectation-threshold theorem
records.doc: Formalizes Tran and Vu's short proof of the Park–Pham theorem resolving the Kahn–Kalai expectation-threshold conjecture. For an ℓ-bounded family of subsets of a finite ground set, it proves the strengthened covering theorem with the explicit constant L = 1000 and derives the threshold bound p_c(F) ≤ K q(F) log₂ ℓ with the explicit witness K = 100000. The supporting library develops finite-set cover cost, level-density, double-counting, binomial-tail, and numeric estimates.
records.informal: If ℓ ≤ N, p lies in [0, 1], and an ℓ-bounded family H has cover cost at least 1/2 - 2^(-(ℓ+2)), then its upset has at least (2/3 + 2^(-(ℓ+2))) choose(N, m) members of cardinality m, where m = floor(1000 p N log₂(ℓ+1)). For m ≤ N this is the corresponding level-density bound; for N < m both cardinalities are zero.

records.name: KasamiCyclicAdditive.carlet_kasami_cyclic_additive_literature
records.entry_name: Carlet's Kasami cyclic-additive conjecture
records.doc: Proves Carlet's cyclic-additive conjecture for the Kasami power function: over every finite field of characteristic two with cardinality 2^n and every k coprime to n, the normalized derivative image has the exact coefficient triple count 2^(2n-3) for all distinct nonzero slopes. The development combines the Müller--Cohen--Matthews permutation theorem, multiplicative character sums, Fourier inversion, and a Fermat-cubic Frobenius-kernel argument.
records.informal: For every finite field K of characteristic two with |K| = 2^n, every k coprime to n, and all distinct nonzero v₁ and v₂ in K, the coefficient triple count of the normalized Kasami derivative image is exactly 2^(2n-3).

records.name: Koethe.KotherConjecture.variants.general_matrix.disproof
records.entry_name: Disproof of the Köthe conjecture (Krempa's matrix form)
records.doc: Refutes Köthe's 1930 conjecture in Krempa's matrix form: there is a ring R (the unitization of a nil algebra of three weighted backward shifts over the algebraic closure of F_2) with a nil two-sided ideal I such that the matrix ideal M_2(I) contains a non-nilpotent matrix. The compared theorem is exactly the negation of the research-open statement `Koethe.KotherConjecture.variants.general_matrix` from Google DeepMind's Formal Conjectures, in every universe. The supporting library proves a multiprojective common-zero theorem via the Segre cone, the Nullstellensatz and Krull's height theorem, a mask-mortality theorem for one-row matrix pencils, a diagonal construction of universal mortal sequences, and a linearization theorem reducing nilness of a three-generator algebra to nilness of its root-row pencils.

records.entry_name: The Komlós and Beck–Fiala bounds with constant 36
records.doc: Proves that finitely many real vectors of Euclidean norm at most one admit signs whose sum has every coordinate bounded by 36, and deduces the Beck–Fiala discrepancy bound 36 times the square root of the maximum vertex degree for finite hypergraphs. The near-invariant distribution uses discrete squared tent weights, and real vectors are handled by coordinatewise truncation toward zero.
records.informal: For a real matrix with arbitrary finite row and column index types, if each column has sum of squared entries at most one, its minimum signed-column discrepancy is at most 36.

records.name: KrafftSieve.mu_min_lt_one_implies_tpc
records.entry_name: A Conditional Sieve Criterion for Twin Primes via Krafft Geometry
records.doc: Introduces an original conditional sieve criterion for the Twin Prime Conjecture. Using a centered modular alignment (termed the Krafft alignment), proves that if the Rayleigh-Ritz quotient over the orthogonal unit sphere satisfies muMin < 1, then a twin prime pair must exist in the corresponding interval.
records.informal: If there are infinitely many intervals where the optimal multidimensional weight achieves a ratio strictly less than 1, then there are infinitely many twin primes. This is a conditional reduction; the hypothesis muMin n < 1 is not established here for any n.

records.name: LeanPool.KrohnRhodes.krohn_rhodes_prime_decomposition
records.entry_name: Aperiodic and simple-group wreath-division towers
records.doc: Constructs a finite recursive wreath-division tower for every finite monoid in universe zero, with finite aperiodic or finite simple-group factors and every simple-group factor a monoid divisor of the original monoid. Implements a variant of the Diekert–Kufleitner–Steinberg local-divisor argument, with reusable monoid and semigroup division, local divisors, action coverings, wreath reassociation, and the Krasner–Kaloujnine group embedding. The endpoint permits arbitrary aperiodic factors and recursive intermediate bases; it does not assert the three-element flip-flop reduction, a single transformation-monoid strong division, or quantitative decomposition bounds.
records.informal: Every finite monoid M in universe zero admits a finite list of finite monoid factors, each witnessed to be aperiodic or a simple group, with DivTowerWreath M factors and every simple-group factor a monoid divisor of M. An empty tower means M divides the trivial monoid. At a nonempty step, M divides F wreath B for a finite action of a finite monoid B that itself has the tail tower.

records.name: GraphCoveringTheory.KuroshStatement.kurosh_decomposition_with_inclusions
records.entry_name: Kurosh and Schreier subgroup theorems via covering graphs
records.doc: Proves the Kurosh subgroup theorem for arbitrary subgroups of indexed free products, with factors given by actual intersections with conjugates of the original factors and with the decomposition maps induced by their inclusions. The development constructs Bass–Serre trees, quotient graphs, graph-of-groups covers, path lifting, and normal forms. It also gives an explicit finite Schreier basis and classifies automorphisms of a finite regular Schreier action by its quotient group. The finite-graph basis infrastructure is reused from LeanPool.FiniteGraphFundamentalGroup.
records.informal: Every subgroup H of an arbitrary indexed free product admits a free product decomposition into a free group and subgroups of H that are intersections with conjugates of the original factors. The isomorphism to H is induced by the actual subgroup inclusions and a homomorphism from the free factor.
